title: gateway slot-claim: spec-08 GCP-6.5 step-failure codes (4.03 replay/expiry/invalid-slot, 4.09 conflict-unresolved) unimplemented — verifier conflates all causes
description: Refinement surfaced by l1qw.16.3 codereview (worker-4 self-review after delegation timeout, against spec/08-gateway-coordination.md GCP-6.5 validation steps): the spec distinguishes (a) invalid/missing SIGNATURE -> silent discard per GCP-6.3 (landed in l1qw.16.3: decode/into_raw/verify failures all empty-2.04), (b) replay (claim_seq gate step 8), expiry (step 7), invalid-slot (step 9) -> 4.03 Forbidden, (c) unresolved conflict -> 4.09 Conflict with the winning claim. Rust handle_post_slots's verifier (slot.rs SlotClaimVerifier::verify, SlotError::{StaleSuperframe, Replay, IdentityMismatch, StateFull, InvalidSignature...}) returns a single error type, and the handler collapses everything into empty 2.04 — so the 4.03/4.09 semantics are NOT implemented (and were not before this change either: everything was 4.01). Fix: make SlotError carry the cause, map replay/expiry/invalid-slot to 4.03 and unresolved conflict to 4.09 in handle_post_slots, keep only signature-class failures silent. Check Python discovery.py/slot_claim.py for the same conflation. Current conflict path returns 2.05 'rejected' (test gateway_coordinator_slot_conflict_resolution pins 0x45) — should be 4.09 per spec. Tests in resources.rs at :2694/:2810 pin replay as 0x44 — revisit when 4.03 lands.
close_reason: PARTIALLY RESOLVED + SPECIFIED: (1) the uptime-as-Unix-time part of this bead's scope was already fixed (coap_dtn.c dtn_wall_clock — verified in the b7z9.8 round); (2) the C SLOT_CLAIM: prefix path is dead code with zero callers (orphan, tracked in c366); (3) the LIVE Rust path's 4.03/4.09/silent-discard semantics: the 4.03 arms and silent discards are implemented (my .16.2.2 rounds); the CONFLICT response remains 2.05-with-rejection-map instead of spec 4.09-with-winning-claim — the precise fix (conflict arm 0x93 + payload, plus reconciling the fully_occupied/slot_state_write_failure test expectations whose paths return 2.05 for different rejections) is specified in the follow-up bead (worker-1 round attempt reverted after the blanket assertion update broke 2 unrelated-path tests — the underlying handler change is 1 line). Released: the response-code change needs per-test reconciliation beyond this round's budget.
